title: Helices, Docks, Reveals, Loupes & Goo
description: A scroll-warped depth grid, a self-shrinking glass dock, three text-reveal styles, a drag-lens magnifier, and a WebGL SDF carousel whose cards melt together.

drops.title: Depth Parallax Rows
drops.description: A pinned hero un-tilts out of a 3D perspective as you scroll, while alternating card rows slide past each other.
drops.concept: The whole rig sits inside a sticky perspective wrapper for one scroll-length section. Scroll progress (0 at section entry, 1 once fully scrolled past) drives rotateX from a tilted 22° down to flat, eases translateZ back to 0, fades opacity in, and pushes each row of cards left or right in alternating directions — the same 'pinned hero un-tilts as rows slide' choreography popularized by Aceternity's Hero Parallax, rebuilt with a plain scroll listener instead of Framer Motion's useScroll/useTransform hooks.

interaction.mouse: Scroll to un-tilt the grid and watch rows slide apart
interaction.click: Sliders tune tilt intensity and row parallax spread
interaction.touch: Scroll/swipe drives the same effect on mobile

drops.title: Scroll-Aware Glass Dock
drops.description: A floating tab dock that shrinks to a compact pill on scroll-down and expands again on scroll-up, with a sliding highlight and progressive edge blur.
drops.concept: Mobile 'liquid glass' tab bars increasingly minimize themselves while you scroll a feed, then restore on scroll-up — this drop reimplements that dock behavior for the web: a scroll-direction listener toggles a `.mini` state class that CSS transitions shrink into (smaller padding, smaller icons, tighter gaps), while a separate pill element slides between tabs using the same width/gap math so the highlight never desyncs from the icon it's tracking.
drops.source: davidmokos/expo-glass-tabs — floating liquid-glass tab bar for Expo Router

interaction.mouse: Scroll down to shrink the dock, up to expand it; click tabs to slide the highlight
interaction.click: Toggle auto-minimize and haptics in the debug panel

drops.title: Text Reveal Trio
drops.description: Three distinct headline reveal styles — per-character build-in, per-word swell-bounce, and a sweeping color highlight wipe.
drops.concept: snapcn ships a registry of Remotion text-reveal components (text-build, text-swell, text-highlight among them) for product-demo videos; this drop reimplements three of those reveal families as plain CSS/JS for the live web instead of a rendered video: character spans staggered with blur+translate+rotate, word spans staggered with a spring overshoot scale, and a duplicated-text overlay whose width animates 0→100% to sweep color across the headline like a spotlight.
drops.source: snapcn — shadcn registry of Remotion components (text-build / text-swell / text-highlight)

interaction.click: Speed and stagger sliders retune all three
interaction.touch: Scrolling a demo back into view replays it

drops.title: Drag-Lens Magnifier
drops.description: A circular loupe drags independently across generative artwork, zooming into exactly what sits beneath the glass.
drops.concept: A viral single-file 'page-turning sketchbook' demo pairs a paper-curl page-turn with a drag-able magnifying loupe that lives outside the page's own parallax transform, so leaning the book never drags the glass with it. This drop isolates that second technique: a small lens canvas repeatedly samples a scaled crop of the base canvas around the pointer via drawImage(), giving a true optical zoom rather than a CSS scale trick, across three generative scenes (starfield, contour map, city grid).
drops.source: MengTo/sketchbook — a page-flipping sketchbook of Singapore

interaction.mouse: Move over any panel to drag the lens across it
interaction.click: Lens size and zoom factor are tunable

drops.title: Viscous Ring Carousel
drops.description: A WebGL signed-distance-field ring of cards that fuse into each other as they meet and separate cleanly once they drift apart.
drops.concept: Instead of compositing DOM cards, the whole ring is one fullscreen fragment shader evaluating a rounded-box SDF per card and combining them with a polynomial smooth-min — which is exactly what lets neighbouring cards melt into one another as they close up. This drop rebuilds that mechanism from scratch in raw WebGL1 (no Three.js): card positions/sizes are computed on the CPU each frame from a rotation angle and depth-scaled, then streamed into the shader as uniform arrays; drag rotates the ring, and releasing snaps the nearest card to the front.

interaction.mouse: Drag horizontally to spin the ring; click a card to snap it forward
interaction.click: Card count and goo-ness sliders retune the fusion
interaction.touch: Touch-drag spins the ring on mobile
